sections.principal_risks: principal risks and uncertainties facing the business. Where possible, processes are in place to monitor and mitigate such risks. Price Risk All our contracts are priced on current market rates, and have a price review every twelve months to ensure our prices remain current with market trends. Credit Risk We continue to operate strict commercial rules that all our applications are agreed before invoices are submitted, which has all but eliminated credit risk Liquidity and Cashflow Risk In line with the above commercial rules, our cashflow is monitored closely to identify risks at an early stage so any cashflow risk can be eliminated before it becomes a problem. We act as a main contractor to the social housing sector which means all our clients meet liquidity checks. Competition in the industry In a saturated market the company is continuously seeking to improve services and carefully manage client relationships. Client saturation The company is actively seeking to diversify its portfolio and identify regions for potential growth. Skilled labour shortages The company has developed an apprenticeship programme alongside succession planning and training to ensure MCP people are available to support business growth. Along with increasing our base salaries for all staff. sections.strategic_report: strategic report for the year ended 31 March 2024. Fair review of the business We aim to present a balanced review of the development and performance of our business during the year and its position at the year end. Our review is consistent with the size and non-complex nature of our business and is written in the context of the risks and uncertainties we face. Accelerating growth through regeneration As a strong, united, and highly motivated family business, we have continued to build on last year’s foundations. Over the last 12 months we have: • Won four new contracts • Invested in support staff to ensure operations are fully supported • Embedded processes and procedures. Our MCP family started the year to continue to build the firm foundations we had started to build last year. We have completed our exit of loss-making contracts and mobilised four new contracts. The mobilisation of new contracts has required an investment from the business hence why our profit has remained static despite the increase in turnover. We are confident that once the new contracts achieve steady state our expect margins will be restored.
